diagnosis_verifications.diagnosis: Metabolic syndrome-driven early type 2 diabetes (insulin-resistance core)
supporting_evidence_verified: Elevated PDW 293 fL indicating platelet activation
evidence_gaps: BMI/waist circumference to confirm central obesity
concerns: DA assigned too low probability for this unifying diagnosis

supporting_evidence_verified: Blood pressure 133/87 mmHg meeting stage 1 criteria

diagnosis_verifications.diagnosis: Iatrogenic Cushing syndrome from chronic high-dose inhaled fluticasone
supporting_evidence_verified: Chronic inhaled fluticasone therapy for persistent asthma
evidence_gaps: Exact inhaled steroid dose, frequency, and duration
Physical exam findings of Cushingoid features
24‑h urinary free cortisol or low‑dose dexamethasone suppression test
concerns: DA over‑estimated likelihood without dose or biochemical confirmation

supporting_evidence_verified: Low HDL and dyslipidaemia could be secondary to hypothyroidism
evidence_gaps: TSH, free T4, free T3 levels
concerns: No thyroid labs provided; probability likely lower than DA estimate

supporting_evidence_verified: Hypertension and metabolic syndrome raise OSA risk

diagnosis_verifications.diagnosis: Early chronic kidney disease / tubular dysfunction
supporting_evidence_verified: Low CO₂ 22.3 mmol/L with high Cl 109.5 mmol/L suggesting non‑anion‑gap metabolic acidosis
concerns: DA omitted this plausible early end‑organ effect

consistency_checks.detail: All severity≥3 abnormalities (HbA1c, low HDL, high PDW) are explained by at least one diagnosis.
DA underestimates metabolic syndrome probability and overestimates iatrogenic Cushing likelihood.
DA omitted early CKD and did not list atherogenic dyslipidaemia as a separate entity.

top_concerns: Under‑estimation of metabolic‑syndrome driven diabetes as primary diagnosis
Over‑estimation of iatrogenic Cushing without steroid dose or cortisol data
Omission of early chronic kidney disease/tubular dysfunction
Lack of key baseline data (BMI, waist, thyroid panel, liver enzymes, renal work‑up, sleep assessment)
Need for ambulatory BP monitoring and lipid‑risk stratification
recommended_primary: Metabolic syndrome‑driven early type 2 diabetes (insulin‑resistance core)
review_summary: The junior Diagnostic Agent captured the central metabolic picture but mis‑weighted probabilities, over‑emphasized inhaled‑Cushing, and missed early CKD and a distinct atherogenic dyslipidaemia label. Adjusted probabilities and added missing entities provide a more accurate, probability‑calibrated differential and guide targeted investigations.
